newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Nervous Aussie dlr waiting on rates window.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Nervous Aussie dlr waiting on rates window.

text.p: AUS$ S/Term range *Support *Restnce *RSI-14 *MA-10 *MA-20
*Offshore range roughly US$0.7416/53
*Aussie dollar stalled above US$0.7410 support level as market braces for possible interest rate cut at the Reserve Bank of Australia's (RBA) 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) announcement time.
*Rumoured options play below US$0.7410 proving good support, but topside capped by selling on moves towards US$0.7450.
*May housing finance data to be released this morning.
A nervous Australian dollar is hamstrung just above US$0.7410 by the fear of a possible rate cut this morning following disappointing June labour force data on Thursday.

A cut is now widely expected but seen as unlikely today at the RBA's 9.30 a.m. window. Instead, the favoured timing for a cut is after the release of June quarter inflation and wages data later in July, or after the August 5 RBA meeting.
However, traders remember the pain caused after they were caught out by the timing of the last two rate cuts on December 11 and May 23, and so no one was taking any chances.
By 7.45 a.m. the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7418/23, slightly down on Thursday's close of US$0.7425/30.
The expectations of local rate cuts were exacerbated by the belief that offshore rates were on a rising trend.
Overnight the Bank of England raised official rates to 6.75 percent from 6.50 percent, the third rise in three months.
Adding to its pressure on the unit was continued subdued performance from commodities. The CRB index fell 1.19 points to 232.70, just above the two year low set earlier this week.
It all added up to a lot of reasons to be a dolar seller at present, with not to many reasons to buy, analysts said.

"Commodities aren't helping is the bottom line. We've got a potential Reserve Bank cut, a potential (U.S.) Fed hike, a potential BOJ hike -- it's hard to excited about the currency going up," Dresdner Australia chief economist Rob Henderson said.
"We think it might spike down if any of these banks move, otherwise it will be capped for a while yet."
However, there was one factor that was providing the dollar with good support at US$0.7410 -- rumours of a large options strangle position written by an Asian name, possibly a central bank.
There have been rumours of similar options positions before, and traders said there were large stop-loss orders just under the US$0.7410 support level if it gives way.
However, With the market already a touch short, the options rumour was enough to keep the dollar above support by preventing further heavy selling.

Should the dollar extend its four month downtrend and break through US$0.7410, it would open the way for a move towards US$0.7300. On the topside, a move above US$0.7550 was needed to counter the downtrend, but this seemed a long way away.

May housing finance data will be released this morning, but it is not expected to have the same impact as the labour force data. Housing has been one of the few sectors of the economy to show signs of improvement in 1997.

After a 12.2 percent rise in April, economists forecasts centre on a 5.7 percent fall. However, this fall is expected to be concentrated in refinancing, with lending for new housing expected to hold up well in the month.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
